issues.display_title: Issue #484: Total Block Profile User Like Corrections API
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 04/08/26

✅ Implementation: Total Block Profile User Like Corrections API

Summary

The existing profile-correction API now returns excluded like counts alongside follower and following corrections.

Route

GET /users/total-block-profile/:username

Registered in src/Routes/V1/UsersRoutes.go:

user.Get("/total-block-profile/:username", Controllers.TotalBlockProfileUser)

Changes

  • Added likes for likes made by blocked or deactivated users.
  • Added likes_banned for likes made by banned users.
  • Joined like, posts, and liker users for both aggregates.
  • Restricted both aggregates to the profile owner's published, non-private posts.
  • Reused the existing combined block/deactivated encrypt list.
  • Added comments explaining that response counters are subtracted from base profile totals.

Existing Counter Semantics

  • follower, following, likes: blocked/deactivated exclusions.
  • follower_banned, following_banned, likes_banned: banned exclusions.

Client calculation:

displayed likes = max(0, ProfileUser.user_count.likes - likes - likes_banned)

File Changed

  • src/Action/V1/Users/TotalBlockProfileUser.go

The route file is documented for discovery but was not changed because the endpoint already existed.

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V1/Users passes; package currently contains no test files.

issues.display_title: Issue #485: Profile User Total Likes API
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 04/08/26

✅ Implementation: Profile User Total Likes API

Summary

The existing profile API now returns published, non-private likes as data.user_count.likes.

Route

GET /users/profile/:username

Registered in src/Routes/V1/UsersRoutes.go:

user.Get("/profile/:username", Controllers.ProfileUser)

Changes

  • Added Models.TotalLikesPerUser mapped to views_total_likes_per_user.
  • Added typed fields for total_likes and total_likes_public.
  • Loaded the target profile user's view row through GORM.
  • Returned TotalLikesPublic as user_count.likes.
  • Defaulted the response value to 0 when no view value is available.
  • Left sl=true unchanged; slim requests skip all user counters.

Files Changed

  • src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileUser.go
  • src/Models/TotalLikesPerUser.go

The route file is documented for discovery but was not changed because the endpoint already existed.

Response Addition

{
  "user_count": {
    "posts": 128,
    "follower": 1200,
    "following": 340,
    "likes": 26500
  }
}

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V1/Users ./src/Models passes; packages currently contain no test files.

issues.display_title: Issue #478: Affiliate GORM Model Query Migration
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 03/08/26

✅ Implementation: Affiliate GORM Model Query Migration

Overview

This document outlines the Affiliate module migration from raw Table(...) queries to GORM Model(...) queries.

Updated APIs:

  • GET /affiliate/list
  • GET /affiliate/categories

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Affiliate/ListAffiliate.go
  2. src/Action/V1/Affiliate/ListAffiliateCategories.go

Implementation Details

1. ListAffiliate.go

Replaced raw table targeting:

Config.DB.Table("affiliate")

with:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Affiliate{})

Both the count query and list query now use the Models.Affiliate table model.

The final list still scans into:

[]Models.AffiliateListItem

This preserves the existing response shape and keeps user_id hidden via the DTO JSON tags.

2. ListAffiliateCategories.go

Replaced raw table targeting:

Config.DB.Table("affiliate_categories")

with:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.AffiliateCategories{})

Both count and data queries now use the Models.AffiliateCategories table model.

3. Removed Manual Mapping Loop

For user role category responses, replaced manual mapping from full category DTO to user category DTO with direct GORM scan:

dataQuery.Select("id, name").
    Order("position ASC, created_at DESC").
    Limit(limit).
    Offset(offset).
    Scan(&userCategories)

This keeps the user response limited to id and name without an extra loop.

4. Response Preservation

Response wrappers, pagination, search behavior, role-specific category output, and encryption behavior remain unchanged.

Verification

Ran:

go test ./...

Result: pass.

Objective

Update Affiliate module APIs to use GORM model-based queries instead of raw Table(...) calls, while preserving existing API response shapes.

Scope

Included APIs:

  • GET /affiliate/list
  • GET /affiliate/categories

Requirements

1. Use GORM Models

Replace raw table targeting:

Config.DB.Table("affiliate")
Config.DB.Table("affiliate_categories")

with model-based queries:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Affiliate{})
Config.DB.Model(&Models.AffiliateCategories{})

2. Preserve Response Shape

  • Keep ListAffiliate response using Models.AffiliateListItem.
  • Keep support role category response using Models.AffiliateCategory.
  • Keep user role category response using Models.AffiliateCategoryUser.
  • Do not expose internal fields that were not previously returned.

3. Avoid Manual Mapping

  • Use direct Scan(...) into response DTOs when selected columns match the response.
  • Do not use manual mapping loops when GORM can scan directly.

Verification

Run:

go test ./...

Expected result: pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #480: Broadcast GORM Model Query Migration
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 04/08/26

✅ Implementation: Broadcast GORM Model Query Migration

Overview

This document outlines the Broadcast module migration from raw table result maps to GORM model-based queries and typed query result models.

Branch:

fix/broadcast-gorm-model-query

APIs Updated

  1. GET /notification/list-broadcast
  2. GET /notification/list-potd
  3. GET /notification/list-broadcast-bookmark/:slug
  4. GET /notification/detail-broadcast-post/:slug

Pure slim handlers in BroadcastSlim.go were intentionally skipped.

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/DetailBroadcastPost.go
  2. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcast.go
  3. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcastBookmark.go
  4. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go
  5. src/Models/BroadcastModel.go

Implementation Details

1. Query Target Updates

Updated Broadcast queries to use GORM models:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Broadcast{})
Config.DB.Model(&Models.Broadcast{}).Table("broadcast b")
Config.DB.Model(&Models.Post{}).Table("posts p")
Config.DB.Model(&Models.Bookmark{}).Table("bookmark b")

This keeps query roots tied to table models while preserving aliases needed by existing joins.

2. Typed Query Result Models

Added typed query containers in src/Models/BroadcastModel.go:

type BroadcastRow struct { ... }
type DetailBroadcastPostRow struct { ... }

These replace DB result containers such as:

[]map[string]interface{}

for joined Broadcast queries.

3. ListBroadcast.go

Changed DB result container to:

var broadcasts []Models.BroadcastRow

The handler still builds the nested response object dynamically because the response contains conditional post, user, and bookmark blocks.

4. ListPotdBroadcast.go

Changed DB result container to:

var broadcasts []Models.BroadcastRow

The existing include filter behavior remains unchanged. Dynamic maps are still used only for response assembly, not for scanning database rows.

5. DetailBroadcastPost.go

Changed DB result container to:

var detailPost []Models.DetailBroadcastPostRow

The response still returns the same nested broadcast, post, and user shape.

6. ListBroadcastBookmark.go

Updated table targets:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Broadcast{})
Config.DB.Model(&Models.Bookmark{}).Table("bookmark b")
Config.DB.Model(&Models.Post{}).Table("posts p")

Existing response DTOs are preserved.

Response Preservation

The migration does not intentionally change response keys, wrappers, pagination, encryption behavior, or include filtering.

Internal fields in typed query containers use json:"-" so they are not accidentally exposed if a struct is returned.

Verification

Ran:

go test ./...

Result: pass.

Task: Broadcast GORM Model Query Migration

Objective

Update Broadcast module non-slim and hybrid APIs to use GORM model-based queries and typed query result models instead of raw table result maps.

Scope

Included APIs:

  • GET /notification/list-broadcast
  • GET /notification/list-potd
  • GET /notification/list-broadcast-bookmark/:slug
  • GET /notification/detail-broadcast-post/:slug

Skipped APIs:

  • Pure slim handlers in BroadcastSlim.go

Requirements

1. Use GORM Models

Replace raw table targeting where practical:

Config.DB.Table("broadcast b")
Config.DB.Table("broadcast")
Config.DB.Table("posts p")
Config.DB.Table("bookmark b")

with model-based query targeting:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Broadcast{}).Table("broadcast b")
Config.DB.Model(&Models.Broadcast{})
Config.DB.Model(&Models.Post{}).Table("posts p")
Config.DB.Model(&Models.Bookmark{}).Table("bookmark b")

2. Avoid map[string]interface{} for DB Results

  • Do not scan database rows into []map[string]interface{}.
  • If the table model does not match a joined query result, add a dedicated query/result model.
  • Keep map[string]interface{} only for dynamic response assembly when the response shape requires it.

3. Preserve Response Shape

  • Do not add table-only fields to responses.
  • Do not expose internal IDs unless the API already returned them.
  • Keep existing nested response objects such as post, user, and bookmark.
  • Keep include-filter behavior in POTD broadcast.
  • Keep encryption response wrappers unchanged.

4. Verification

Run:

go test ./...

Expected result: pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #481: Implementation: Notifications GORM Model Query Migration
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 04/08/26

✅ Implementation: Notifications GORM Model Query Migration

Overview

The Notifications module was migrated from raw table queries and map-based database scan targets to GORM model-based queries and typed query result models.

APIs Updated

  1. GET /notification/lists
  2. GET /notification/total-unread
  3. GET /notification/list-month

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Notifications/ListNotifications.go
  2. src/Action/V1/Notifications/ListNotificationMonth.go
  3. src/Action/V1/Notifications/TotalUnreadNotification.go
  4. src/Models/NotificationsModel.go
  5. src/Models/NotificationsModel_test.go

Implementation Details

1. Query Target Updates

Notification and post queries now use model references:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Notifications{}).Table("notifications n")
Config.DB.Model(&Models.Post{})
Config.DB.Model(&Models.TotalUnreadNotification{})

Aliases remain only where existing joins require them.

2. Typed Query Result Models

Added these query result types in src/Models/NotificationsModel.go:

type NotificationQuery struct { ... }
type NotificationPostQuery struct { ... }
type TotalUnreadNotification struct { ... }

TotalUnreadNotification.TableName() maps its model to views_total_unread_notifications.

3. List Notifications

Joined notification rows are scanned into []Models.NotificationQuery. Post details are scanned into Models.NotificationPostQuery. Dynamic maps remain only for conditional slim/full response assembly.

Existing pagination, notification-type filters, visibility rules, Redis exclusions, panorama conversion, and encryption behavior remain unchanged.

created_at is normalized to UTC and serialized with the Z suffix so local and development environments return the same timestamp representation.

4. List Notification Month

Joined notification rows and optional post details now use typed query results. The handler still assembles its response dynamically to preserve pw behavior and conditional post fields.

5. Total Unread Notification

Unread totals are scanned into []Models.TotalUnreadNotification. The total is calculated from the typed Total field instead of a map type assertion.

6. Tests

src/Models/NotificationsModel_test.go verifies unread-total JSON field names and nullable post IDs in notification query results.

Response Preservation

No route, response wrapper, response key, pagination rule, filter, or encryption format was intentionally changed.

Verification

Ran:

go test ./...

Result: pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #482: Implementation: Likes GORM Model Query Migration
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 04/08/26

✅ Implementation: Likes GORM Model Query Migration

Overview

The Likes module database reads were migrated from raw table queries and map scan results to GORM model roots and typed query models.

APIs Updated

  1. GET /posts/list-like/:sid
  2. GET /posts/total-block-like/:sid
  3. GET /users/check-like-post/:sid
  4. GET /comments/list-like/:commentSid

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Likes/CheckLikePost.go
  2. src/Action/V1/Likes/ListLikePost.go
  3. src/Action/V1/Likes/ListLikeComment.go
  4. src/Action/V1/Likes/TotalBlockedLikePost.go
  5. src/Models/LikeModel.go
  6. src/Models/LikeModel_test.go

Implementation Details

1. GORM Query Roots

Queries now use Models.Post, Models.Comment, Models.Like, and Models.LikeComment as roots. Existing aliases remain where joins require them.

2. Typed Query Models

Added:

type LikeTarget struct { ... }
type LikedUser struct { ... }
type LikeAggregate struct { ... }
type TotalLikesPerComment struct { ... }

These replace map scan targets for post/comment lookups, liked-user rows, and aggregate results.

3. Safer Lookup

Post slug or ID selection uses parameter binding instead of concatenating route input into a SQL condition.

4. Response Preservation

Dynamic maps remain only for response assembly. Existing filters, pagination, order, roles, visibility rules, status codes, messages, and encryption wrappers remain unchanged.

5. Frozen Slim Compatibility

Slim behavior is legacy compatibility scope. Its routes, sl parameter, conditional logic, response shapes, and encryption paths must remain unchanged. No future model-query migration should intentionally edit them.

6. Tests

src/Models/LikeModel_test.go verifies liked-user and aggregate JSON output.

Verification

go test ./...

Result: pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #483: Centrifugo GORM Model Query Migration
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 04/08/26

✅ Implementation: Centrifugo GORM Model Query Migration

Overview

The Centrifugo module was migrated from raw token_centrifugo table and SQL calls to GORM operations backed by Models.TokenCentrifugo.

APIs Updated

  1. GET /centrifugo/token
  2. GET /centrifugo/typing-comment/:sid

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Centrifugo/TokenCentrifugo.go
  2. src/Action/V1/Centrifugo/TypingComment.go

Implementation Details

1. Token Lookup

Both handlers now query through:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.TokenCentrifugo{})

The lookup scans into the typed Models.TokenCentrifugo model and uses RowsAffected to detect whether a token exists.

2. Token Update

The raw SQL UPDATE was replaced with:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.TokenCentrifugo{}).
    Where("user_id = ?", userId).
    Updates(...)

The token and updated_at fields are updated together.

3. Token Creation

The raw SQL INSERT was replaced with Create using a typed Models.TokenCentrifugo value. The authenticated user ID is parsed into its UUID model type.

4. Typing Comment

The token existence check now uses the same GORM model query. The Centrifugo HTTP publish request remains unchanged.

Behavior Preservation

JWT creation, authentication, response fields, status codes, error messages, external publish payload, headers, and routes were not intentionally changed.

No slim route, parameter, condition, handler, or response was modified.

Verification

Ran:

go test ./...

Result: pass.
